title: Morgan Stanley upgrades EU chip sector to overweight and highlights top-rated stocks - Yahoo Finance UK
text: Morgan Stanley upgrades EU chip sector to overweight and highlights top-rated stocks Vicky McKeever · Business reporter 20 January 2026 4 min read ASML.AS 2330.TW ASM.AS BESI.AS Morgan Stanley ( MS ) has upgraded its view on the European semiconductor sector to "overweight" and highlighted three top-rated stocks operating in the space. Analysts at the US investment bank said in a note published on Tuesday that they had become "more constructive" on European Union equities more broadly, coming into the new year. They said that this was partly down to "EU equities' breakout of its formerly structurally widening valuation discount range" versus the US, as of the end of the year. In addition, they said this was due to a "sharp rise in diversification inflows into EU equities with investor interest pointing to further flows into key pockets of the market". Morgan Stanley's analysts said that while the "recent Greenland-related tariff escalation complicates this picture somewhat ... we note incremental tariff exposures are highly idiosyncratic, rather than broad-based." They added that potential impact to companies' earnings per share (EPS) are "counterbalanced by recent upwards revisions to US GDP [gross domestic product] growth". Read more: FTSE and European winners and losers a year into Trump's second term In addition, the analysts said that "developments are likely to reinforce Europe's determination to assume a greater responsibility for its own security & strategic autonomy, likely propelling not only Defence spending, but the broader European reform agenda." US president Donald Trump has threatened to impose new 10% tariffs from 1 February on eight European countries over opposition to his proposed takeover of Greenland. He said in a social media post at the weekend that this levy would rise to 25% on 1 June, with these tariffs payable "until such time as a Deal is reached for the Complete and Total purchase of Greenland". Morgan Stanley's analysts said that "in the event of further escalation, we note such events historically tend to drive sharp but short market declines, with recoveries ensuing thereafter". Top-rated semiconductor stocks In their note, the analysts said that they were upgrading the EU semiconductor sector to a "strategy overweight". The analysts said that their global semiconductors team argued that for 2026, the risk in the AI capital expenditure (capex) cycle is "execution and transition, not demand". "Potential future capex cycle bottlenecks thus become the winners," they said, adding that this included the EU semiconductor capital equipment industry, particularly in the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) space. Dutch company ASML ( ASML.AS ) is the only company that makes EUV lithography systems and is one of Morgan Stanley's top picks for EU equities. The investment bank's analysts have an "overweight" rating on the stock and recently raised their price target on ASML to €1,400 (£1,221). ASML shares are up 49% over the past year and are trading at €1,115 at the time of writing. Story continues Morgan Stanley equity analyst Lee Simpson said the bank had raised its price target "off the back of expectations for a stronger 2027". "Larger 2027 foundry and memory capex, as well as better than feared China demand, drives our conviction for higher FY27 earnings," he said. Fellow Dutch company ASM International ( ASM.AS ) was also named as a top EU stock pick by Morgan Stanley's analysts. They have a price target of €800 on the overweight-rated stock, which is up 12% over one year and trading at €697 per share at the time of writing. ASMI is also an equipment maker, though its technology is involved in a different part of the chipmaking process to ASML. ASMI supplies wafer processing equipment to semiconductor makers. Morgan Stanley equity analyst Nigel van Putten said that TSMC ( 2330.TW ), the world's biggest contract chipmaker, had validated his team's bull case on ASMI by "raising capex significantly in an effort to ease supply constraints on leading edge foundry capacity". Last week, TSMC reported fourth quarter earnings and guidance that topped analyst estimates . The company also increased its capex budget for 2026 to a range of $52bn (£38.7bn) to $56bn. Morgan Stanley analysts also highlighted another Dutch company, BE Semiconductor Industries ( BESI.AS ), in their note. They also have an "overweight" rating on the BESI, which supplies "semiconductor assembly equipment". Shares in the company are up more than 15% over one year and are trading at €169 at the time of writing.
